intro: Many Hindu families tell stories at home. Two favorites are about Krishna and Ganesha. Children hear them at festivals and at bedtime.
Many Hindus honor Krishna and Ganesha as forms of God. You will hear their stories. You will hear how families celebrate them.
By the end, you can retell two stories. You can name two festivals. You can say what each story helps children think about.
bigQuestion: What do the stories families tell help children learn?

timeline.t: Little Krishna grows up in a cowherd village
Krishna sneaks butter and shares it with friends
A great storm comes to the village
Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill to keep everyone dry
Ganesha and Kartikeya start a race around the world
Kartikeya flies away on his peacock
Ganesha walks around his parents and says they are his world
Families tell these stories at Janmashtami and Ganesh Chaturthi

words.d: a cowherd boy in the stories, honored by many Hindus as a form of God
a person who takes care of cows
to give some of what you have to others
the hill Krishna lifts in the story
a deity with an elephant head, honored by many Hindus as the remover of obstacles
something that is in your way

test.q: Where does Krishna grow up in the stories?
choices: In a garden with a peacock
test.why: Krishna grows up in a cowherd village.

test.q: What does Krishna lift in the storm?
test.why: Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill like an umbrella.

test.q: Whose head is like an elephant's?
What do many Hindus call Ganesha?
test.why: Many Hindus call Ganesha the remover of obstacles.

test.q: How does Ganesha win the race?
test.why: Ganesha says his parents are his world.

test.q: Which idea goes with Krishna and the hill?
test.why: Krishna lifts the hill to keep everyone safe.

write.prompt: Draw and tell. Pick one story: Krishna and the hill, or Ganesha and the race. Draw the most important part. Tell a grown-up what happens and what families say it teaches.
tips: Tell what happens first, next and last.
Say "Families say..." when you tell the lesson.
Use a word from this unit, like share or obstacle.
